ns2:course.label: US Citizenship Comparatively
ns2:course.description: Examines the racial, gendered, and sexualized aspects of US citizenship historically and comparatively. Interdisciplinary course taught from a humanities perspective. Readings draw from critical legal studies, history, literature, literary criticism, and ethnography. Same as AFRO 215, AIS 295, GWS 215, and LLS 215. Prerequisite: One of: AAS 100, AAS 120, AFRO 100 AIS 101, GWS 250, LLS 100.
ns2:course.sectionDegreeAttributes: Hist&Philosoph Perspect, and US Minority Culture(s) course.
